audio_cues.text: Three bills.
Thirty days.
First, Maya's car broke down.
Then came an urgent dental bill.
And just when she thought the month couldn't get worse, a pipe leaked beneath her kitchen sink.
The total?
Two thousand two hundred dollars.
But when Maya opened her savings app afterward, she didn't feel proud.
She saw how much her balance had fallen and thought, I've gone backwards.
Here's why she hadn't.
Once the card was paid off, she opened a separate savings account and set up an automatic transfer of fifty dollars every week.
Fifty dollars a week, for fifty-two weeks, gave her two thousand six hundred dollars.
But this time, she had an answer.
The money was already there.
Three bills in thirty days.
Two thousand two hundred dollars gone.
Four hundred dollars left.
An emergency fund is supposed to get smaller when there's an emergency.
Using it isn't failure.
That's literally the job it was hired to do.
What bill would have shaken you a year ago, but feels more manageable today?
I'd love to hear it in the comments.
